insights.headline: He treats other people's silence as a complete and sufficient signal, absolving him of needing to ask what they need.

analysis.pattern: You have a reflex that turns every loss into proof of a plan, applied instantly rather than earned.
analysis.description: Your framing is "everything happens for a reason, right, like I fully believe that" — a sincere conviction, not something you call a coping mechanism. But the pattern across your telling is that this frame lands within a sentence of the loss itself, every time: "God had to close that door. Literally." on the house, and "I think God clears the table before He serves the meal" on Kayla. Four different losses across four different decades get sealed the same way, in seconds, not after time to sit with them. That timing is what makes this worth naming — not the belief itself, but its speed.

analysis.prediction: If asked directly what you do with a setback that has no silver lining yet, you'll supply one before the conversation ends rather than say you're still waiting on it.
